_why: The plan is evidence only if it demonstrably predates the outcome. Commit dates can be set to anything; GitHub's merge timestamp and a Solana block time cannot. This file binds the two and is written SEPARATELY so T3.plan.json stays byte-identical to what was frozen.

WRITTEN AFTER THE FACT, AND THAT IS A RE.statement: This record was created on 2026-09-26, two days after the run, because it was never written at freeze time. T6's was written the same evening. Nothing in it is asserted from memory — every field below is read from GitHub's API, from git, or from devnet block times — but a reader should know the file did not exist while the pool was filling.
WRITTEN AFTER THE FACT, AND THAT IS A RE.whatThatDoesAndDoesNotCost: It costs nothing in verifiability: the merge time, the plan hash and the block times are all recoverable by anyone, from sources this repository cannot rewrite. It costs the property that the record itself was contemporaneous, which T6's has and this does not.
WRITTEN AFTER THE FACT, AND THAT IS A RE.howItWasCaught: reconcile.ts refused the pool as UNFROZEN and called it a FAIL by itself. The tool was right and the gap was mine.

THE CLAIM THIS RECORD EXISTS TO MAKE.statement: THE PREDICTION WAS FROZEN BEFORE ANY ENTRY LANDED — and NOT before the pool existed.

THE WEAKER STANDARD, STATED PLAINLY.so: T3 does NOT hold T6's and T2R's standard, which is that the plan was frozen before the pool it ran on existed. Pool 29 was opened by the settlement daemon two and a half hours before PR 171 merged. T3 holds the weaker standard: frozen before any seat registered.
THE WEAKER STANDARD, STATED PLAINLY.whyItIsStillEvidence: The plan names no pool — poolId and poolPda are both null in the frozen bytes, and still are. Nothing about pool 29 could have shaped the prediction: its tier, entry price, pot, minimum field and fill window are the tier's standard values, which the plan states independently, and the prediction is about ALLOCATIONS and COUNTS, not about the pool. Knowing pool 29 existed conveys no information the plan could have used.
THE WEAKER STANDARD, STATED PLAINLY.whyItIsWeakerAnyway: That argument is a reader's judgement, not a mechanical fact. T6's ordering needs no argument at all: the pool could not exist until we acted, and we did not act until the freeze merged. This one needs the reader to accept that pool identity is irrelevant to the prediction. It is, but it has to be said rather than shown.

pool.parametersChecked: tier 0, entry 100000000, pot 4000000000, min_seats 40, and a 43200-second fill window — every one as the frozen plan states it.
